howto.name: Paste your .env text
howto.text: Paste the contents of a .env file into the .env input box, replacing the sample that loads with the page. There is no file upload. Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped, each line is trimmed, and Windows line endings are accepted.

howto.name: Read the validation report
howto.text: The Validation report updates as you type and lists each finding by line number, counting every line, including blank and comment lines. It never repeats a name or a value from your text, so use the line number to find each one. Errors are highlighted in red. When nothing is flagged, the report reads No obvious .env issues found.

howto.name: Fix the errors
howto.text: An error means a line is not a usable KEY=value pair, and nothing else on that line is checked. A line with no equals sign gets not a KEY=value line (no = sign). A name that is not ASCII letters, digits and underscores starting with a letter or underscore gets not a KEY=value line (invalid variable name), as the sample's BAD NAME=value does on line 4.

howto.name: Review the warnings
howto.text: Warnings flag a repeated key (duplicate key, first set on line N), an empty value, a value containing spaces or tabs that is not wrapped in matching quotes, and a short secret: value looks short for a secret appears when a name containing SECRET, TOKEN, KEY or PASSWORD has a value under 12 characters.

howto.name: Copy the report
howto.text: Copy puts the report on your clipboard, one finding per line with an [OK], [WARN] or [ERROR] prefix. It copies the report, not your .env text, so make the fixes in your own file.

faq.q: What does the report say for the sample?
faq.a: The sample has four lines: API_URL=https://privatools.me, SECRET_KEY=change-me, FEATURE_FLAG=true and BAD NAME=value. The copied report is two lines: [WARN] Line 2: value looks short for a secret, because change-me has 9 characters, and [ERROR] Line 4: not a KEY=value line (invalid variable name), because names cannot contain spaces.

faq.q: Why is a line with spaces around = flagged?
faq.a: The value is everything after the first =, so PORT = 8080 has the value " 8080" and gives Line 1: quote values that contain spaces. An inline comment does the same, as in PORT=8080 # web port, because # only starts a comment at the beginning of a line. Write PORT=8080, and wrap values that need spaces in quotes.

faq.q: How does the short-secret check work?
faq.a: It looks for SECRET, TOKEN, KEY or PASSWORD anywhere in the name, in capitals only, so api_key is not checked while MONKEY is. A leading and a trailing quote are removed before counting; 12 characters pass and 11 are flagged. An empty value under such a name gets both the empty-value and the short-secret warning.

Each repeat gets a warning such as Line 2: duplicate key, first set on line 1. However often a key repeats, every warning points back to the line that set it first. The key itself is not named; the two line numbers lead you to it.

faq.q: Are export lines and multi-line values supported?
faq.a: No. export API_TOKEN=... is read as a variable named export API_TOKEN and reported as not a KEY=value line (invalid variable name). Each line is checked on its own, so every continuation line of a multi-line value, such as a PEM key, is judged as a separate entry: most get not a KEY=value line (no = sign), and a base64 line ending in = can look like a name with an empty value.

No. It checks syntax and a few hygiene rules. It does not recognize real credentials, compare the file with a .env.example, or know which variables your app needs. Use a dedicated secret scanner before committing credentials.

faq.q: Will it reveal my secrets to PrivaTools?
faq.a: No. Validation is plain JavaScript in the page; the tool makes no network request with the text and does not save it in browser storage. The report never repeats text from your file, not even names: each finding is a fixed message with line numbers, so a copied report holds none of your keys or values.
